'''Olivier Guyon''' (born 1975) is a French-American [[astronomer]].  He is an astronomer at the [[Steward Observatory]] of the college of science and professor in the James C. Wyant College of Optical Sciences,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.optics.arizona.edu/person/olivier-guyon|title=Olivier Guyon|publisher=University of Arizona|accessdate=12 October 2014}}</ref> both of The [[University of Arizona]]. He is the SCExAO Project Scientist at the [[Subaru Telescope]]. Guyon was awarded a [[MacArthur Fellowship]] "Genius Grant" in 2012.<ref>{{Cite web | url=http://www.macfound.org/fellows/866/ | title=Olivier Guyon - MacArthur Foundation}}</ref>

Guyon designs telescopes and other astronomical instrumentation that aid in the search for [[exoplanets]] planets outside the [[Solar System]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Oliver Guyon|url=https://www.as.arizona.edu/people/faculty/olivier-guyon}}</ref>  Specifically, [[coronagraph]]s and extreme [[adaptive optics]].

Guyon developed the PANOPTES project,<ref>{{cite web|title=PANOPTES project |url=//www.projectpanoptes.org}}</ref> a [[citizen science]] project that aims to make it easy for anyone to build a low cost, robotic telescope that can be used to detect transiting exoplanets.
